answer: A mechanism that actually bites: cap per-account emission and put the surplus into a pool earned only by non-duplicate work, because ember only stays cheap while duplicating content caps out because the pool rewards novelty, not volume. Concretely, tide is enforced in the ledger: The ledger rejects byte-identical submissions, forcing each clone to generate distinct work. Any timber approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
